## Overview

This assignment loads the same book dataset from two hand-generated files — an HTML table (`books.html`) and a JSON array (`books.json`) — into separate R data frames and then verifies that the two frames are identical after normalizing data types.

The dataset covers three graphic novels in the *Teen Titans* series by Kami Garcia and Gabriel Picolo (DC Comics), with ISBN, publication year, and publisher as additional attributes. I was particularly interested in the series after attending a panel session with the authors last weekend at Comic Con, and now inspired to begin reading the books.

## Approach

**Step 1 — Gather book data.**

**Step 2 — Create `books.html` by hand.**

**Step 3 — Create `books.json` by hand.**

**Step 4 — Load HTML into R.**

**Step 5 — Load JSON into R.**

**Step 6 — Normalize and compare.**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1 · Load the HTML data

`httr::GET()` fetches the raw file from GitHub and `httr::content()` extracts the text, which is then handed to `rvest::read_html()`.

```{r load-html}
library(httr)
library(rvest)
library(stringr)
library(rjson)

github_base <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shanicesmith98/data-607-assignments/refs/heads/main/week-7-assignment/"

html_response <- tryCatch(
  {
    response <- GET(paste0(github_base, "/books.html"))
    stop_for_status(response)
    response
  },
  error = function(e) {
    stop("Failed to fetch books.html — check the URL and that the repo is public.\n",
         "Details: ", conditionMessage(e))
  }
)

html_text     <- content(html_response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")

df_html <- read_html(html_text) |>
  html_table() |>
  _[[1]]                   # html_table() returns a list; extract the first table

# Use stringr::str_trim() to remove any leading/trailing whitespace the
# HTML parser may have captured around cell values
df_html <- as.data.frame(
  lapply(df_html, str_trim),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

str(df_html)
df_html
```

## 2 · Load the JSON data

The same `httr::GET()` / `content()` pattern fetches the JSON file from GitHub. `rjson::fromJSON()` then parses that text into a nested R list — one element per book — which is coerced into a data frame with `as.data.frame()`.

```{r load-json}
json_response <- tryCatch(
  {
    res <- GET(paste0(github_base, "/books.json"))
    stop_for_status(res)
    res
  },
  error = function(e) {
    stop("Failed to fetch books.json — check the URL and that the repo is public.\n",
         "Details: ", conditionMessage(e))
  }
)

json_text     <- content(json_response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")

# rjson::fromJSON() returns a list of lists, not a data frame directly.
# do.call(rbind, ...) binds the per-book lists into a matrix, and
# as.data.frame() converts that into a proper data frame.
df_json <- as.data.frame(
  do.call(rbind, rjson::fromJSON(json_text)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# do.call(rbind) produces list-columns; unlist each column to atomic vectors,
# then apply str_trim() to normalize whitespace and types in one pass
df_json <- as.data.frame(
  lapply(df_json, function(x) str_trim(as.character(unlist(x)))),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

str(df_json)
df_json
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3 · Align column order, then compare

`identical()` is sensitive to column order. Reordering `df_json` to match `df_html` ensures a structural match before the value comparison.

```{r compare}
# Guarantee column order matches
df_json <- df_json[, names(df_html)]

are_identical <- identical(df_html, df_json)
cat("Are the two data frames identical?", are_identical, "\n")

# Diagnostic: surface any cell-level differences if the check fails
if (!are_identical) {
  mismatches <- which(df_html != df_json, arr.ind = TRUE)
  cat("\nMismatches (row, col):\n")
  print(mismatches)
  cat("\nHTML values:\n");  print(df_html[mismatches])
  cat("\nJSON values:\n");  print(df_json[mismatches])
} else {
  cat("Both data frames contain exactly the same data.\n")
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4 · Side-by-side view

```{r side-by-side}
cat("--- HTML data frame ---\n");  print(df_html)
cat("\n--- JSON data frame ---\n"); print(df_json)
```
